children.name: Government Regulation

reasoning_box.text: Fair. Policy direction is a clear and well-documented tailwind — the teaser sets out IRDAI's "Insurance for All by 2047" (2022), the National Health Claims Exchange (2023), the Bima Trinity of Bima Sugam, Vistaar and Vahak (2024), and 100% insurance FDI with composite licences under the new Insurance Bill (2025), alongside Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and ABHA interoperability which our external sources cite as the primary driver of Indian digital health growth. Zyla is also not itself a licensed entity: it does not underwrite, dispense or operate a hospital, so it captures the tailwind without carrying the licensing burden, and it holds SOC 2 and ISO 27001. BUT IT IS NOT GOOD, FOR TWO REASONS. It employs doctors delivering remote clinical advice, which brings it inside the Telemedicine Practice Guidelines; and it processes sensitive personal health data at very large scale (2L+ paid lives) under a DPDP Act regime whose operating rules are still bedding in. A licensed-adjacent sector with periodic compliance obligations and a known change in the pipeline whose impact is not yet clear is precisely the Fair anchor. ASK: the DPDP compliance assessment and consent architecture; medical-council registration status of the clinical team; the SOC 2 report and ISO 27001 certificate with dates; and the data-processing agreements with insurer clients and the liability they carry. Supporting evidence recorded at Evidence & Workings row 72.
